maria: quick heads-up — ran a profiling pass on prod-dedicated with torch.compile + CUDA graphs. Observed kernel selection flip depending on seqlen (8 -> 32) and KV cache state. Short seqs suddenly pick a slower matmul path, latency +35%. Anyone seen this pattern?

aj: ugh yeah. seen similar when graph capture merges cached-KV and new-token paths. can you paste the profile?

maria: attaching trimmed nvprof snippet and a tiny repro below. noticed kernel names flip: `attention_fused_v1` -> `matmul_cutlass_128x128` for seqlen 8 when capture happens at runtime.

```
# nvprof excerpt
GPU activities:
    123.45ms  attention_fused_v1  (seqlen=32, batch=1)
     87.12ms  attention_fused_v1  (seqlen=64, batch=1)
    195.30ms  matmul_cutlass_128x128  (seqlen=8, batch=8, kv_cached=true)
```

maria: repro sketch:
```
model = TransformerLayer(...)
compiled = torch.compile(model)
# capture path
with torch.cuda.graphs.capture_stream(stream):
    out = compiled(x, kv_cache)
```
If kv_cache present and batch merges, CUDA graph capture picks the matmul fallback.

sanjay: hmm — sounds like dynamic shape got folded into the graph capture. torch.compile tries to optimize and the kernel selector/autotuner picks per-shape best kernel. When capture happens with cached KV (smaller seq per step but larger internal matmul due to concat), cutlass wins in perf model but is slower for our microbatched traffic.

aj: also check batching heuristic — we saw cases where the runtime concatenates cached KV + incoming tokens into a single matmul with larger batch dims, which can change tiling and force a different kernel. autotuner uses (seq_len, head_dim, sm_arch, batch) to choose. if any dimension crosses threshold, it flips.

ryan: possible mitigations:
- avoid capturing across shapes: capture per effective-seq (use per-step capture)
- add a capture guard that forces the non-graph path when kv_cache_present and seq < threshold
- pin the kernel via an env flag to force fused attention for short seqs (temporary)

perf-bot: previous runbook note: see perf-tests/2025-06-autotune-seqlen-thresholds (internal). there is a known threshold at seq==16 where autotuner prefers cutlass on Ampere for head_dim=64.

maria: thanks — i can try forcing fused attention env var. does anyone have the quick env flag?

aj: set REDWOOD_RUNTIME_KERNEL_OVERRIDE=attention_fused_v1 (at process start). it forces kernel choice for that op. use for canary only.

sanjay: long-term fix: update kernel selector to be capture-aware. when graph capture is enabled, treat capture shapes as "pinned" and prefer kernels with stable performance across microbatching (or pick conservative fused kernels). also, add a post-capture reprofile step to validate chosen kernels.

ryan: agree. small patch: during capture, annotate the graph with "capture_context" and feed a hint to the kernel picker: prefer stable_fused. PR idea: runtime/kernelselect: add capture_hint bool + fallback_penalty param.

maria: I ran a quick canary: set override and latency drop for short seqs back to expected. pushing a small canary now. deploy-bot, can you note deployment?

deploy-bot: canary started: infra/dedicated-prod canary id=c-20260312-17. routing 5% traffic. rolling update on runtime v2.41.2. :rocket:

maria: next steps:
- aj/sanjay to prototype selector change (capture-aware)
- ryan to draft PR with fallback_penalty config and env override support documented
- i'll run a microbenchmark sweep (seqlens 1..128, batch 1..16) with kv_cache on/off and attach results to the ticket

aj: i'll take the selector prototype. will add unit tests for seq thresholds and for kv_cache concat shapes.

ryan: i'll open initial PR WIP today. mark it experimental behind REDWOOD_EXPERIMENTAL_KERNEL_HINTS.

maria: also we should update the batching heuristic: avoid mixing cached-KV heavy requests with fresh long-seq requests in the same capture window — that mixing is what triggers the tile change. maybe route cached flows to a small-latency pool.

perf-bot: scheduling a perf-job: job/1791240010-kernel-stability-sweep queued. will post results in this thread when done.

maria: great, thanks everyone. saving logs and will attach the full flamegraphs in the ticket. :thumbsup:

ryan: FYI — if you need a quick workaround, set REDWOOD_DISABLE_CUDAGRAPHS=true to bypass capture entirely for affected pools until selector patch lands.

maria: noted. i'll prefer kernel override first so we keep capture benefits. will update thread after perf-job.

perf-bot: job/1791240010 finished: initial matrix shows 28% median regression at seq<=16 when capture happens with kv_cache=true. full CSV uploaded to s3://redwood-perf/canaries/1791240010.csv

maria: perfect — that's the delta we saw locally. opening ticket RD-3456 with repro and perf artifacts.

aj: thanks. ping if you want pair-debug on the selector heuristics tomorrow.

maria: will do.
